Rashi on Eruvin 21b:10:1.hebrew: ולהג הרבה - המלעיג עליהן, ביגיעות בשר נידון:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:10:1.english: And much study - One who mocks them is judged with weariness of the flesh.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:11:1.hebrew: כל ההוגה בהן - בכל שעה שאדם מחזר בדברי תורה, מוצא בהן טעם:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:11:1.english: Whoever meditates upon them - Whenever a person reviews words of Torah, he finds flavor in them.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:12:1.hebrew: הגרסי - שם מקום. ל"א — שהיה טוחן גריסים:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:12:1.english: HaGarsi - The name of a place. Another explanation: That he would grind groats.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:13:1.english: And my life depends on your life - For I have only what you give and provide for me.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:15:1.english: In his youth - For he was able to endure hardship and affliction.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:16:1.hebrew: שלמה תיקן עירובי חצירות - וגזר שלא להוציא מרשות היחיד לרשות היחיד חבירו, לעשות סייג והרחקה לאיסור תורה, שלא יבוא להתיר מרשות הרבים לרשות היחיד. והיינו דכתיב: ״ואיזן וחקר תיקן משלים״ — שעשה אזנים לתורה, כאזני כלי שאוחזין אותו בם:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:16:1.english: Solomon instituted the eiruvin of courtyards - And he decreed not to carry out from [one] private domain to the private domain of his fellow, to make a fence and a safeguard for the Torah prohibition, so that one would not come to permit [carrying] from the public domain to the private domain. And this is that which is written: “And he pondered [ve’izen], and searched out, and set in order many proverbs” (Ecclesiastes 12:9) — that he made handles [oznayim] for the Torah, like the handles of a vessel by which one grasps it.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:16:2.hebrew: וידים - נטילת ידים, לעשות סייג לטהרות:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:16:2.english: And hands - [This refers to] the washing of hands, to make a safeguard for [ritually] pure foods.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:18:1.hebrew: כרכים - מקום שווקים הן, וישוב גדול, ורגל רוכלין וסוחרין מצויה שם. לפיכך, גזל ועריות נוהג בהן:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:18:1.english: Large cities - They are a place of marketplaces and a large settlement, and the foot of peddlers and merchants is commonly found there; therefore, robbery and licentiousness are prevalent in them.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:18:2.hebrew: השדה - בני בגא ועובד אדמה, ועוסקין בתורה מתוך דוחק:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:18:2.english: [Into] the field - [These are] people of the countryside and tillers of the soil, and [yet] they engage in Torah [study] amid hardship.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:1:1.english: The first-ripe [figs] - Choice figs that are quick to ripen.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:20:1.hebrew: סמדר - גדול מפרח, כך משנה מפורשת יותר מן המקרא:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:20:1.english: The grape blossom [semadar] - [This stage] is more developed than a flower [peraḥ]; so [too], the Mishnah is more explicit than Scripture.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:20:2.hebrew: הנצו הרמונים - גדלו כל צרכן, וכבר הנץ גדל סביבותיו, כעין שומר שיש לאגוזים קטנים:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:20:2.english: “The pomegranates are in flower” - They have reached their full growth, and the blossom has already grown around it, like a protective covering that small nuts have.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:22:1.hebrew: אגמריה בסימני טעמים - קבע לה מסורת וסימנין, בין בתיבות המקרא, בין בגירסא של משנה:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:22:1.english: He taught it with the accentuation marks - He established for it a tradition and mnemonic signs, both in the words of Scripture and in the recitation of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:23:1.hebrew: ועשה לה אזנים - שתיקן עירובין וידים, וגזר על השניות לעריות, כדמפרש ביבמות (כא.). וע"י כך אוחזין ישראל במצות, שנתרחקו מן העבירה, כדרך שנוח לאחוז בכלי שיש לו בית יד משאין לו:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:23:1.english: And made handles for it - For he instituted [the laws of] eiruvin and [the washing of] hands, and decreed against secondary [degrees of] forbidden relations, as is explained in Yevamot (21a). And through this, Israel hold fast to the mitzvot, in that they are distanced from transgression, just as it is easier to hold a vessel that has a handle than [one] that does not.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:4:1.hebrew: שאוגדות - קושרות פתחן לצורך בעליהן, שאינן נבעלות לאחרים. אוגדות — לשון אגודה. ל"א: שמגידות פתחיהן — כשרואה דם, אומרת לבעלה ויפרוש הימנה:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:4:1.english: Who bind - They tie [shut] their opening for the sake of their husbands, as they do not have relations with other [men]. Ogedot is an expression of binding [agudah]. Another version: “Who tell of their openings” — when she sees [menstrual] blood, she tells her husband so that he will separate from her.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:5:1.english: New - The words of the Scribes.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:5:2.english: Also old - [These are] words of the Torah.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:5:3.english: My Beloved, I have laid up - And I have kept all these for You, for [the sake of] Your Name.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:7:1.english: [Was it] given on separate occasions - That this [mitzvah] should be new and that [one] old.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:7:2.english: Words of the Scribes - [These are the] new [ordinances], which were newly instituted in every generation to erect a fence and a safeguard.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:8:1.hebrew: ויותר מהמה - לעיל מיניה כתיב: "דברי חכמים כדרבונות" — אלו דברי תורה שנמסרו למשה על פה, שנחלקו בה חכמי ישראל לאחר שנתמעט הלב ושכחו, כדכתיב בסיפיה דקרא: "נתנו מרועה אחד" — זה משה. וכתיב בתריה: "ויותר מהמה בני הזהר" — ממה שניתן בסיני בכתב, שהוא עיקר, בני, הזהר באלו שבעל פה, שגם הם עיקר; אלא לכך לא נכתבו — שאין קץ לעשות ספרים הרבה בכל אלה:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:8:1.english: And more than these - Prior to it, it is written: “The words of the wise are like goads” (Ecclesiastes 12:11) — these are the words of Torah that were transmitted to Moses orally, concerning which the Sages of Israel disputed after understanding diminished and they forgot, as it is written at the end of the verse: “they were given from one shepherd” — this is Moses. And it is written after it: “And more than these, my son, be careful” (Ecclesiastes 12:12) — [even more] than [with] that which was given at Sinai in writing, which is primary, my son, be careful with these [teachings] of the Oral Torah, for they too are primary. Rather, it is for this reason that they were not written down: because there is no end to making many books with all of these.

Rashi on Eruvin 21b:8:2.hebrew: עשה ולא תעשה - יש בהן שאין בהם חיוב מיתה, אבל דברי סופרים — חייבין מיתה על כולן, כדכתיב (קהלת י׳:ח׳): ״ופורץ גדר ישכנו נחש״:
Rashi on Eruvin 21b:8:2.english: Positive and negative [commandments] - There are among them [commandments] that do not carry liability to death; but [regarding] the words of the Sages, one is liable to death for all of them, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 10:8): “And whoever breaches a fence, a snake shall bite him.”

Tosafot on Eruvin 21b:14:1.hebrew: מוטב אמות מיתת עצמי - אף על גב דבפ' קמא (ד' יז.) אמר: "ארבעה דברים פטורין במחנה: רחיצת ידים" — וכל שכן במקום סכנה — מחמיר על עצמו היה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 21b:14:1.english: "It is better that I should die my own death" - Even though in the first chapter (17a) it says: "Four things are exempt in an [army] camp, [one of which is] washing of the hands" — and all the more so in a situation of danger — [Rabbi Akiva] was being stringent upon himself.

Tosafot on Eruvin 21b:16:1.hebrew: בשעה שתיקן שלמה עירובין ונטילת ידים - אף על גב דתיקן נמי שניות, כדאמר בפרק שני דיבמות (ד' כא.) — הא דלא חשיב הכא, משום דלאו בבת אחת תיקן, ואחר בת קול תיקן. ומדכתיב: "איזן וחקר תיקן משלים הרבה", משמע נמי שהרבה תקנות עשה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 21b:16:1.english: At the time that Solomon instituted eiruvin and the washing of hands - Even though he also instituted sheniyot [secondary forbidden relations], as [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Yevamot (21a), the fact that it does not enumerate [them] here is because he did not institute [them] at one time, and he instituted [them] after the Divine Voice [emerged]. And from that which is written: "He weighed, and sought out, and set in order many parables" (Ecclesiastes 12:9), it also implies that he made many enactments.

Tosafot on Eruvin 21b:9:1.hebrew: מפני מה לא נכתבו - וגם בהלכה למשה מסיני לא נתנו, כדי שלא ישתכחו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 21b:9:1.english: "Why were they not written" - And [why] were they also not given as a halakhah le-Moshe mi-Sinai, so that they would not be forgotten?
